title: Unfair Advantage,  Moat Builder
subtitle: A competitor launches something similar. An investor asks 'what stops someone from
useWhen: copying this?' You don't have a clear, confident answer. Your business is growing but feels fragile.
howToUse: Warren Buffett's concept of an economic moat describes a sustainable competitive advantage that protects a business from competition the way a moat protects a castle. The five types of moat are: Network Effects (the product gets better as more people use it), Cost Advantage (you produce at lower cost than anyone), Switching Costs (customers are locked in by habit, data, or integrations), Intangible Assets (brands, patents, licences), and Efficient Scale (a market so small only one player can profitably serve it). Most businesses have weak or no moats. Building one is a strategic choice.
steps: Identify which of the five moat types you currently have, be honest.
Rate each on a scale of 1–5 for strength. Anything below 3 is not a real moat.
Identify which moat type is most achievable given your current position.

Build moat-widening into your product and business roadmap deliberately. Identify what protects you that competitors cannot easily copy Amazon's unfair advantage wasn't its website , it was the proprietary logistics infrastructure it built over 15 years. When AWS launched, Amazon was already operating data centres at a scale no competitor could match affordably. The moat wasn't the product. It was the underlying capability that took a decade and billions to build and that no startup could replicate quickly. IN PRACTICE
origin: Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway annual letters — moat concept, 1980s onwards
promptBody:
Act as a competitive strategy advisor focused on economic moats.
My business                 :  [DESCRIBE WHAT YOU DO AND WHO YOU SERVE]
Stage                             :   [REVENUE STAGE - PRE / EARLY / SCALING]
Assess my moat across all five types:
NETWORK EFFECTS   :  Does value increase with more users?
COST ADVANTAGE     :   Can I produce cheaper than competitors?
SWITCHING COSTS   :   How painful is it for customers to leave?
INTANGIBLE ASSETS :   Do I have brand, IP, or licence advantages?
EFFICIENT SCALE       :   Am I in a market too small for competition?
Rate each 1–5. Identify my strongest moat and the fastest moat I could build
from my current position. Give 2 specific actions to widen my strongest moat.
Network Effects
Value increases with user base growth.
Cost Advantage
Lower production costs enhance
competitiveness.
Switching Costs Competitive
High costs deter customers from switching. Protection
Intangible Assets

protection.

proTip:
Network effects are the most powerful moat but the hardest to build. If your product has
any element where more users create more value even indirectly, design your product
and go-to-market specifically to accelerate that loop. Most founders have a network
effect they don't know they have.
